messages:
jessica_ae: Hey team — ACME's POC window closed today. They asked us to fully deprovision the POC environment and confirm data/key cleanup. Need: invalidate hosted API keys, teardown Dedicated pool (pool-ACME-42), and remove VPC peering for the Private deployment. Can infra + security confirm steps and ETA?

dan_se: Thanks — tagging infra + sec. Quick question: do they want keys rotated or fully revoked? Also need to confirm whether any logs or artifacts need to be preserved for audits before teardown.

rory_infra: For Dedicated pool teardown I can run the standard teardown workflow. Steps: 1) drain connections, 2) snapshot any requested artifacts (if requested), 3) run `redwoodctl teardown --pool-id pool-ACME-42 --confirm` which triggers autoscaling group termination and frees GPUs, 4) remove billing assignment. If you want me to kick it off I need the approval window (we should do it during low-traffic). ETA ~2 hours once started.

jessica_ae: They said no snapshots needed, just ensure no customer data retained. Re keys: they want keys invalidated permanently. Also they asked for a short attestation we deleted everything they had access to.

tina_sec: Security notes: we must revoke hosted API keys, delete any KMS data keys tied to the tenant if using envelope encryption, and confirm logs retention window. Per our default POC policy: request logs & metrics are retained 30 days; trace-level request bodies are retained 7 days unless otherwise requested. If ACME needs evidence, we provide a one-page attestation with timestamps and actions. I will prepare the attestation once infra confirms actions.

rory_infra: Got it. Plan:
- Hosted API keys: revoke in Console and via admin API: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/keys/revoke -d '{"key_id":"acct-ACME-poc"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'` — this invalidates tokens immediately.
- Dedicated pool: `redwoodctl teardown --pool-id pool-ACME-42 --confirm --no-snapshot` -> triggers `deploy-bot` job.
- Private/VPC: remove peering and customer route prop: `aws ec2 delete-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0abcd` (we'll coordinate with networking team). Also remove any peered subnets from our firewall allowlist.
I will start Hosted key revocation now if you confirm.

jessica_ae: Confirm — please revoke keys now and then I authorize pool teardown after revoke completes. Also ask networking to schedule VPC peering removal; ACME prefers the removal in same maintenance window.

deploy-bot: pool-teardown-job submitted for pool-ACME-42, job_id=jt-98341, requested_by=rory_infra. Current status: queued.

rory_infra: Hosted API key revoke initiated -> admin API returned 200. Keys are invalidated. Verified by attempting a simple curl to the hosted endpoint using the old key (expected 401). I ran:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer acct-ACME-poc" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' | jq .
```
Response: 401 Unauthorized. Keys revoked.

tina_sec: Confirming KMS cleanup: no customer data keys found in our tenant KMS path except the ephemeral data-key used for the session; I rotated and deleted the ephemeral key material. Audit record: `sec-audit-2026-03-18-7842` created. Logs retention: standard POC retention applies (30/7). If ACME requires full deletion of request bodies earlier, that's a separate request; they didn't ask for it.

rory_infra: Teardown job jt-98341 started. Progress: draining clients -> 30% -> shutting down serving instances -> 80% -> releasing GPUs -> 95% -> completed. Pool-ACME-42 removed from cluster. Billing assignment cleared.

jessica_ae: Thanks — can you attach the attestation PDF and the job IDs to send to ACME?

tina_sec: Attestation draft done. Includes key revoke timestamp, KMS deletion id, pool teardown job id jt-98341, and logs retention statement. I'll add the audit record id and sign-off. Sending to jessica to review. :white_check_mark:

jessica_ae: Received. Sending to ACME now, marking POC as deprovisioned on CRM. Closing thread unless anything else pops up. :pray:
